newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam approves eight new cabinet members.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam approves eight new cabinet members.

text.p: Vietnam's National Assembly approved plans for a sweeping cabinet reshuffle on Wednesday, bringing in eight newcomers but rejecting at least one nominee.
State television said the assembly had approved plans for changes to a total of 12 ministerial or ministerial level posts.
It did not say why consent had been given for only eight.
But informed government sources said the remaining positions were expected to be finalised over the next few days with one or more existing ministers likely to be reassigned to new portfolios.
The assembly rejected Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet's choice for transportation minister, but gave no reasons for the decision.

Those approved for new cabinet posts were Tran Xuan Gia as Minister for Planning and Investment, Le Minh Huong as head of the powerful Interior (Police) Ministry and Nguyen Sinh Hung as Finance Minister.

Pham Gia Khiem was accepted as minister for Science, Technology and the Environment, Nguyen Khoa Diem as Culture and Information Minister, Ta Quang Ngoc as Marine Products Minister and Lai Van Cu as Minister for the Government Office.
The ministerial-level position of head of the Organisation and Personnel Committee of the Government went to Do Quang Trung.
Western analysts in Hanoi said the reshuffle was broadly in line with expectations and amounted to a wide-ranging ministerial change.
Under Vietnam's political system the new ministers are unlikely to be formally appointed before the current session of the National Assembly draws to a close in about a week.
Vietnam's cabinet comprises more than 30 people, including ministers, heads of state commissions and other government bodies.
The reshuffle is the first major shake-up in Vietnam since a landmark Communist Party Congress in late June.
